A 25-year-old G1P0 woman at 15 weeks of pregnancy presents to the clinic with complaints of fatigue
lasting three weeks. She has experienced minimal weight gain during pregnancy due to daily nausea
and vomiting, which have lessened since entering the second trimester. Currently, she reports nausea
with vomiting occurring several times per week. Her medications include prenatal vitamins. Vital signs
are stable, and physical examination reveals a comfortable patient with no acute distress, a non-tender
abdomen, and a gravid uterus consistent with gestational age. Laboratory results are as follows: |
**Laboratory Test** | **Serum Value** | | --- | --- | | Hemoglobin | 10 g/dL | | MCV | 75 fL | | Iron | 39
mcg/dL | | Ferritin | 9 ng/mL | | Total Iron Binding Capacity | 427 mcg/dL | | Vitamin B12 | 500 pg/mL | |
Folate | 10.0 ng/mL | What is the most appropriate treatment for this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Oral
folate (B) Oral B12 (C) Parenteral folate (D) Oral vitamin C supplementation (E) Combination therapy
with oral iron and folate (F) Erythropoietin therapy (G) Intramuscular B12 (H) Intravenous iron (I) Blood
transfusion (J) Oral iron
 A. Oral B12
B. Oral folate
C. Parenteral folate
D. Intramuscular B12
E. Combination therapy with oral iron and folate
F. Intravenous iron
G. Erythropoietin therapy
H. Blood transfusion
I. Oral vitamin C supplementation
J. Oral iron
